name: Channel 0
from: Channel 0: a broken greyscale TV with pink missing-texture glitches; every channel says the same thing.
hook: Every channel tells you the same thing: keep watching.
pitch: One remote, one button. A greyscale TV flips between channels, and pink missing-texture glitches spread with every flip, out of the set and into the room. There is no way to win. The only real choice is whether to put the remote down.
minute_check: Yes: the gesture is the game.
build_check: Yes: eight channel loops and an overlay.
scope: Eight channels at most. Decide whether putting the remote down is possible; it is the one real choice.

brief.goal: None stated: keep flipping channels. Each channel tells you to rely on the TV.
brief.ending: The vignette closes, the pink glitches spill out of the set into the room, and the TV takes over.
brief.theme: Dependence as a gesture: the only thing you can do is ask the TV for more. The pink placeholders are the gaps the company leaves.
brief.look: Hand-drawn static, chicken-scratch lines, greyscale with pink and black missing-texture checks.

prov.bug: Flip again, the next channel will explain it.
prov.nit: If there is no way to win, what does the player choose? Can they put the remote down?

refs_lit: A man consumed by a broadcast. The body-and-screen horror you are drawing on.
Your glitch motif. Use the real pattern deliberately: magenta and black, 2x2.
Kentucky Route Zero, WEVP-TV interludes (Cardboard Computer, 2013-2020)
Interactive television as a piece in itself, with choices that change little and mean a lot.
omni_gameplay_prompt: Hand-drawn scratchy greyscale psychological game (#161616 and #d8d8d8) with vivid magenta-and-black (#ff4fd8) missing-texture checkerboard glitches. Steady first-person view facing a bulky vintage CRT television in a dim sketchy bedroom; a hand in the lower corner clicks a remote control. Each click snaps the CRT screen through jittering hand-drawn broadcast static, and glowing magenta-black checker squares spill outward from the glass bezel onto the surrounding wallpaper. Continuous unbroken gameplay shot, no scene cuts, no gibberish text. Use the reference image for TV framing and palette. Sound design: heavy plastic remote clicks, CRT static hiss, rising low drone. No dialogue.
